column5: The type of a marker runs to the end of its line, or to a `null`, a `not null` or a `->` that ends it.
column6: Old: "runs to the end of its line, but for a `null` or `not null` that ends it, so nothing else may follow it there".  False: a `-- param:` marker is `@name [type] [null | not null] [-> [json] CSharpType]`, and the arrow ends the type too (src/SqlSource/Parsing/Markers/SqlMarkerScope.cs, ReadParam and TrySplitArrow).  Step 3 of the PostgreSQL fix says the same.  Found by the accuracy review

column5: The tool describes only `SELECT` (without `INTO`), `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `VALUES` and `TABLE`, with `WITH` around any of them.
column6: Old: "PostgreSQL prepares only `SELECT` (without `INTO`) ...", which the same section contradicts: PostgreSQL 15 and later prepare `SELECT ... INTO`, and the tool refuses it on every version.  The list is what the tool describes, as the help line of the error says (src/SqlSource.Tool/Describing/Postgres/PostgresErrors.cs).  Found by the accuracy review
